figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Ring expansion catalyzed by TropC/SpoC in the biosynthesis of tropolone natural products. (a) Representative natural products using
tropolone as the biosynthetic precursor. (b) Biosynthesis pathway for stipitaldehdyde (1). (c) The proposed radical rearrangement (uncoordinated
substrate), semipinacol rearrangement (substrate bis-coordinated to Fe), and radical rearrangement (substrate monocoordinated to Fe and covalent
to K110) for the ring expansion in the biosynthesis of tropolones. The methyl group marked in the black box represents that it came from SAM and
was eventually inserted into the tropolone ring. The hydroxyl group (brown-red) was introduced into the compounds by TropB. The red circles
represent the free radicals generated during the reactions. A simplified schematic diagram of the six-coordinate Fe was used.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Substrate recognition mode in the cavity of SpoC. (a) SpoC-catalyzed biosynthetic pathway of 1. (b) The overall structure of SpoC in
complex with NOG in chain A. Protein is shown as cartoon (light gray), with NOG shown as stick (yellow), and the Fe surrogate Mn ion is shown
as sphere (dark purple). Mesh represents a simulated annealing composite mFo-DFc omit map contoured at 2σ; for more details and an enlarged
view of the mesh, see Figure S19. All of the O and N elements are colored red and blue, respectively. (c) Details of the binding site of NOG in
SpoC. H2O is shown as nb_sphere (red). Mn ion is colored dark purple here. (d) Model of SpoC-α-KG-substrate 3 complex, substrate 3 is colored
pink and α-KG is colored yellow. (e) Catalytic activity assays of the wild-type (WT) and mutants of SpoC, using 3 as substrate and α-KG as
cosubstrate. Recombinant proteins were purified from E. coli strains. Relative enzyme activities for the formation of 1 compared to SpoC WT are
presented as the mean ± s.d. from three independent replicates.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Structural and biochemical evidence for imine adducts in SpoC. (a) The binding details of product 1 in the active site of SpoC. C
elements of 1 are colored green. All of the O and N elements are colored red and blue, respectively. (b) Mesh of 1 and K110. The mesh is
simulated annealing composite mFo-DFc omit map contoured at 2σ and colored gray. The program phenix.composite_omit_map24 is used to
generate this map. It was run with a simulated annealing method, and the annealing type is “Cartesian”. The map type is mFo-DFc. (c) 1 adopts a
binding mode similar to that of the α-KG analogue NOG. (d) Formation of imine adducts after the incubation of SpoC with substrate 3 under
reaction conditions. Two distinct adducts were observed: (i) unreacted substrate 3 forms an imine linkage with K110 of SpoC (+164 Da); (ii) the
substrate 3 was reacted under catalytic conditions, yielding product 1-SpoC adduct (+162 Da). The K110A variant showed no modification under
identical conditions. More detailed figures are provided in Figures S33 and S36−S37.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. QM computation results of SpoC-catalyzed reaction pathways to generate stipitaldehyde (1) (INT5). The top-right panel displays the
full QM calculation model, including all amino acids and water molecules within the computational environment. For clarity, subsequent transition
states (TS) and intermediates (INT) only present Fe-coordinating residues and the residue covalently bound to the substrate, with full model
details provided in Figures S42−S43. Full computational details are described in experimental procedure 9 (Supporting Information).
